# ankra_security_disposition (Resource)

A vulnerability disposition: an acknowledgement or an accepted risk over the finding occurrences its selector matches. The selector is derived once, from the anchoring occurrence and the scope; the reason and the lifecycle can change in place. Destroying the resource revokes the policy; revocation is the platform's only removal and keeps the policy in the audit history. A policy revoked outside Terraform is planned for recreation. The counterpart of `ankra security dispositions create`, `update` and `revoke`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Acknowledge a finding on the one workload it was seen in.
resource "ankra_security_disposition" "frontend_net" {
  occurrence_id = "8f0c5a1e-2d4b-4c7e-9a31-5b6d7e8f9a0b"
  scope         = "workload"
  disposition   = "acknowledged"
  reason        = "Not reachable from outside the cluster"
}

# Accept the risk of a finding across every cluster running the add-on.
# An accepted risk needs a review deadline within a year.
resource "ankra_security_disposition" "ingress_cve" {
  occurrence_id             = "3c2b1a09-8f7e-4d6c-b5a4-938271605f4e"
  disposition               = "accepted_risk"
  reason                    = "Mitigated by the WAF rule set"
  expires_at                = "2027-03-31"
  expire_when_fix_available = true
  revoke_reason             = "WAF rule removed"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `disposition` (String) `acknowledged` or `accepted_risk`. An accepted risk needs `expires_at`. Changing it replaces the disposition.
- `occurrence_id` (String) Finding occurrence the policy is anchored on (from `ankra security finding <id>`). The platform never returns it, so it is not read back; after an import the configured value is recorded without a change. Changing it replaces the disposition.
- `reason` (String) Why the finding is acknowledged or its risk accepted, kept for audit (at most 2000 characters).

### Optional

- `allow_unmatched` (Boolean) Store the policy even when its anchor no longer matches any occurrence. Only read at creation, so changing it replaces the disposition. Defaults to `false`.
- `expire_when_fix_available` (Boolean) End the disposition the moment a fixed version appears. Defaults to `false`.
- `expires_at` (String) Review deadline, an RFC 3339 timestamp or a `YYYY-MM-DD` date; it must be in the future, and within a year for an accepted risk. It can be moved in place, but removing it replaces the disposition because the platform cannot clear a deadline.
- `revoke_reason` (String) Reason recorded when Terraform revokes the policy on destroy. Changing it only changes what a later destroy records. Defaults to `Revoked by Terraform`.
- `scope` (String) Selector scope: `organisation_addon` (the default: the occurrence's add-on across the organisation, which needs a confident add-on attribution), `workload` (the one workload the occurrence was seen in) or `image` (the image digest, wherever it runs). Changing it replaces the disposition.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the policy was created (RFC 3339).
- `created_by` (String) Ankra user id that created the policy.
- `id` (String) Identifier of the disposition policy.
- `match_health` (String) Whether the selector currently matches: matched, unmatched or fix_available.
- `matched_occurrence_count` (Number) Occurrences the policy currently matches.
- `selector` (Attributes) What the policy matches, as the platform derived it. Members the scope does not pin are null. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--selector))
- `selector_hash` (String) Hash of the canonical selector.
- `status` (String) Lifecycle status: active, expiring, fix_available, mitigated, unmatched or expired.

<a id="nestedatt--selector"></a>
### Nested Schema for `selector`

Read-Only:

- `addon_slug` (String) Add-on the policy is pinned to (scope `organisation_addon`).
- `cluster_id` (String) Cluster of the pinned workload (scope `workload`).
- `cve_id` (String) CVE identifier.
- `image_digest` (String) Pinned image digest (scope `image`).
- `package_name` (String) Package name.
- `package_type` (String) Package ecosystem.
- `workload_kind` (String) Kind of the pinned workload (scope `workload`).
- `workload_name` (String) Name of the pinned workload (scope `workload`).
- `workload_namespace` (String) Namespace of the pinned workload (scope `workload`).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Dispositions are imported by policy id. The anchoring occurrence is not
# returned by the platform; the configured occurrence_id is recorded on the
# next apply without changing the policy.
terraform import ankra_security_disposition.ingress_cve 5d1e8a4c-7b2f-4e3a-9c6d-0f1e2d3c4b5a
```
